The Genesee County Circuit Court was established in 1836, soon after Michigan became a state. It was initially a circuit court that covered Genesee County and several other neighboring counties. However, as Michigan’s population grew, the court system evolved, and the Genesee County Circuit Court became a standalone court.

Jurisdiction of Genesee County Circuit Court

The Genesee County Circuit Court has jurisdiction over civil cases, criminal cases, and family cases. It has the authority to hear and decide cases involving amounts over $25,000, criminal offenses that carry a penalty of over one year in jail, and family matters such as divorce, custody, and child support.

Judges in Genesee County Circuit Court

The Genesee County Circuit Court has ten judges who are elected to six-year terms. The judges are responsible for hearing cases, issuing orders, and making decisions in the best interest of justice.

The Genesee County Circuit Court handles various types of cases, including:

Criminal Cases

Family Cases

The court handles family cases such as divorce, child custody, and child support.

Genesee County Circuit Court Processes

The Genesee County Circuit Court follows standard legal processes to hear and decide cases. The processes include:

Jury Selection

In criminal cases, the defendant has the right to a trial by jury. The court follows a rigorous process to select a jury, ensuring that the jurors are unbiased and have no personal interest in the case.

Pre-Trial Hearings

The court conducts pre-trial hearings to ensure that both parties have sufficient evidence to present in court.

Trials

The court conducts trials to hear evidence, examine witnesses, and make a decision in the case.

Sentencing

In criminal cases, the court imposes a sentence on the defendant if found guilty. The sentence can include jail time, fines, or probation.
